title: Tricky (high-frequency) words
examples: Teacher, what makes these words tricky?
Can we practice reading these words quickly?
Do I need to sound out the word 'said'?

explain.say: Some words you see a lot have a part that sounds different. You learn these words by sight.
Look at the word the. The e at the end sounds different from the e in egg.
Look at the word said. You hear e in the middle, but you see ai.
Look at the word was. The a sounds like the o in dog. The s sounds like z.
These words are called sight words. Read them many times, and you will know them quickly.

faq.q: Why are these words called tricky words?
faq.a: Part of the word sounds different from its letters. So it is easier to learn the whole word by sight.

faq.q: Do I have to sound out every word?
faq.a: No, for these special words, we just look and say them right away. We learn to read them instantly. (asks) Should I sound out 'was'?
asks: Do I always sound out words?

faq.q: How many tricky words should I learn?
faq.a: You learn them slowly, one small group at a time. Practice makes these words feel easy to read. (asks) Is this for forever?
asks: How many tricky words should I learn?
Will I learn all of them?

faq.q: Can I use these words in my writing?
faq.a: Yes, you use them all the time when you write sentences. They help your stories sound more natural. (asks) Are these words for reading only?
asks: Are these words for reading only?
Can I use these words in my writing?

faq.q: What is the difference between a tricky word and a normal word?
faq.a: A normal word follows the sounds you learn in phonics. A sight word has a part that sounds different, so you learn it by sight.
asks: How is it different from other words?

facts: Sight words are words that appear very often in writing.
Learning them by sight helps reading become faster.
These words do not always follow standard phonics rules.
Practising them helps you read more smoothly.

quiz.say: Read this sentence. Which word fills its gap?
quiz.why: I sat on the mat. The word the fits in the gap.

wrong.0: Read it aloud with was, and the sentence sounds wrong.
wrong.2: Read it aloud with said, and the sentence sounds wrong.

quiz.say: Read the sentence. Tap the right spelling for the gap.
quiz.why: This word is spelt s, a, i, d. You hear e, but you write ai.

wrong.1: Sed matches the sounds, but this word is spelt with ai in the middle.
wrong.2: In this word, the a comes before the i.

quiz.say: Read the sentence. Tap the right spelling for the gap.
quiz.why: This word is spelt w, a, s. The a sounds like o, and the s sounds like z.

wrong.0: Woz matches the sounds, but this word is spelt with a and s.
wrong.1: Wos matches the sounds, but this word is spelt with an a.
